title: Quasi-coherence of the canonical annihilator of an ideal power
statement: Let X be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], I and F sheaves of O_X-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], and ι : I → O_X a monomorphism. Assume I is quasi-coherent of finite type and F is quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent]. For n ≥ 0 let j_n : P_n → O_X be the recursive power inclusion [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk]. Define A_n(W) as the submodule of s in F(W) such that for every V ⊆ W and b in P_n(V), j_n(b) times s restricted to V is zero. This restriction-stable family is a sheaf by gluing in F and testing products locally. Its inclusion is the actual subtype inclusion. Then this explicitly constructed sheaf A_n is quasi-coherent.

source.place: Lemma 01PO, proof of clause (1), applied to powers in Lemma 01PQ

proof.text: Reuse powers_affine_sections from CoherentSupportVanishingIdealNilpotence via a proof-only import all. This already proved private helper applies to every quasi-coherent module map to the structure module, without Noetherian or monicity hypotheses. It proves quasi-coherence of the recursive power object and identifies its affine inclusion range with the nth power of the original affine range, including exponent zero. Reuse finite_sections_of_finiteType from QuasicoherentFiniteTypeAffine to see that the original ideal sections over an affine open form a finite module. Mathlib Submodule.fg_range and Ideal.FG.pow make every power range finitely generated.

For a quasi-coherent module map j:P -> O_X, define J(U) as the range of j on each affine open. Naturality proves the forward inclusion in the principal-open ideal-extension identity. For the reverse inclusion, lift a section b of P on D(f), after multiplying by a power of f, to a section on U using the affine localization theorem. Its image under j is in the extended ideal; the restriction of f is a unit, so multiplication by its power can be cancelled for ideal membership. These explicitly constructed affine ideals form IdealSheafData J. Reuse the proved ideal_qc helper from CoherentSupportVanishingIdealNilpotence with the identity isomorphism to show J.toModules is quasi-coherent. Its injective section map identifies its sections on U with the finitely generated ideal J(U), giving finite sections; the affine finite-type criterion on the full affine cover shows J.toModules is of finite type.

Show that the actual canonical annihilator inclusion has affine image exactly the sections killed by J(U). One implication tests the defining condition on U itself and the identity restriction. Conversely, cover any smaller open V by its affine subopens W. Ideal extension along W subset U puts J(W) in the ideal of scalars killing the restricted section. Naturality sends every local section of P on V into J(W), so its product with the restricted section vanishes on every W. Sheaf separatedness makes the product vanish on V, giving a section of the canonical annihilator. Apply annihilator_subsheaf_quasicoherent to this actual inclusion and the finite-type ideal data J, then specialize j to the nth recursive power inclusion.
